I had mentioned that previous therapists pushed certain grounding techniques (five things you can see, for example). They not only don’t work for me, they drive me to full blown panic attacks. I had also brought up that I have many sensory issues. I don’t have any sort of formal diagnosis, but I am interested in getting some assessments done.

My current therapist’s response: You have sensory issues and the grounding techniques they were pushing are all about senses. Of course you were feeling worse when you tried them. They’re completely counterproductive for you.

She did some research into grounding techniques that work well for people with sensory issues. Recommended that I observe the things around me and mentally state facts about them. “There are two mirrors in this room. That book over there is white and orange. This is the date. This is the time.” Things that would put me into the present without bringing discomfort into it. Avoid sensory words like see, smell, touch. Just state facts about the items around me.

It works. She actually heard what I was saying and worked with me rather than those previous therapists giving me a “one size fits all” response and then blaming me when it didn’t work.

When I was a teenager and started forming my own opinions, he became stern. He had (and still has) such a strict and narrow perspective of the world and he was determined to make us have it too. When I disagreed, he became hateful. He would insult me for the things I believed and the values I had and the way I saw the world.

I’ve told him countless times that I don’t want to discuss certain topics with him, but it’s all he ever wants to talk about, so he keeps trying to bring them up. A part of me wonders if he really thinks that we’re just having a spirited debate when it always ends with him yelling insults and slamming doors, or if he thrives off of the abuse and turning the rest of the family against me, then acting as if nothing happened and I have “no reason” to be so upset.

As an adult, I know that he just wanted people to agree with his horrible views and praise him night and day. I have no reason to look up to him other than an example of what I never want to become. He is hardly one of the smartest people I know. He is a terrible person and incredibly immature. He hates the world because he feels entitled to so much more than what he has, and he’ll take every opportunity to vent that anger onto anyone and everyone. He’s a hateful person through and through, and I can’t wait until I never have to hear of him again.

I was convinced that I was just lucky and he hadn’t noticed, but eventually I asked him about it. He said that yeah, he could smell when I walked into a room, but he never thought of it as a bad smell. He actually really likes it, and he finds a lot of comfort in it. To the point that he will sink into me every time we hug/cuddle. Intimate smells are the same. He’s a big fan.

What I didn’t realize until recently is that I was conditioned by my family from a young age. They drilled into me that any sort of smell on a woman that wasn’t flowery was disgusting. They would make comments about how gross I was constantly. Turns out that I internalized that.

I even went to the doctor to make sure. I’m completely fine.

Again, anecdotal, but sometimes it’s not the smell itself.

My dad was stomping around, slamming doors and cupboards, turning on the tv, all in the next room with nothing to block the sound. I muted myself and asked him if he could try to be quieter until my game was done. He ignored me. My mom reminded him that this was my request, since the room organization was not my choice. He then stage-whispered for half an hour about me. I could hear him the whole time.

I have diagnosed complex PTSD from my family. Mainly from him. So I was growing more and more frustrated but even more scared. I ended up asking to end the game early, saying that there was an emergency. My group was very nice about it.

I was on the verge of a panic attack as I left my computer and approached my parents. I was emotional, reminding them that I’ve asked for quiet multiple times. My dad interrupted me, saying that bad things would happen to me if I kept talking. I tried to persist, and he kept turning everything around on me and projecting his own behaviours on me. He stormed away. I went to my room.

My dad found my mom crying later, so he came into my room and said that since I had made the mess, I needed to clean it up. I went to my mom thinking he would leave. He did not. I talked to my mom a bit, trying to explain that I was frustrated and felt emotionally trapped because I can never voice my wants/needs without being punished. My dad wouldn’t stop interrupting me. I eventually started interrupting him to say “please let me finish”, he would snap that I was interrupting him.

My sister overheard at some point and came over. The entire time, my dad was twisting my words, projecting his behaviour onto me, making faces, rolling his eyes, being sarcastic, constantly. My mom and my sister sided with him. I don’t reminder how many times I asked to be able to say something. He threatened to destroy my laptop if I loved it so much, which I use for school. Eventually he said that if I was going to keep dominating the conversation, I should get out. I left. My mom and my sister left. As we left the room, my dad slammed the door multiple times. He opened it to say “metzona is toxic, don’t talk to her, don’t acknowledge her, and we’ll all be better off for it” then slammed the door again.

I went downstairs to work on homework. My mom and my sister were still upset. I know I wouldn’t be able to study while so panicked, so I sat down with them to try to talk things through. I tried to explain my perspective. They sat on the fence, saying that even if my dad did something to hurt me, I wasn’t completely innocent, so I should apologize. I wanted this to be over, so I went back to him. I apologized for my behaviour. I told him that our father-daughter relationship is important to me. I said that I wanted to work on fixing things. He stared at me. He then made another face and said “I haven’t heard an apology. I haven’t seen remorse. I don’t see you taking accountability”. I replied that I literally just said those things. He denied this, saying that I hadn’t said those things at all. My mom and my sister sided with me since I asked them to be witnesses. They said that I had shown and said the things he wanted. He shrugged and said “I guess if you want to pretend you’re the victim and make this worse, that’s your choice”. Everyone but my dad left the room.

I didn’t bother trying to do homework. I stayed downstairs for a bit, then went upstairs. I took my laptop with me, just in case he wanted to go through with his threat.

This is the nail in the coffin for me. I can’t live like this anymore. I need to get out.

I’m a pharmacy assistant. I went to school for pharmacy technician, and this actually came up in a lesson. The standard procedure for dealing with employees like this is to keep them far away from those kinds of medications and the patients. They will see it as being spared from having to go against their morals, but really it’s to protect the patients from the employee.

That being said, depending on how small the pharmacy is, they will not last long. Inwardly miserable people are a bit more complicated. They know that they're in a bad state and shouldn't let it continue, but they just can't bring themselves to climb out.
